title: Paint all 532 pin tips of a TacTip tactile skin white, bringing every side of its dome to the paint without smearing
instruction: Paint every pin tip on the TacTip skin white without getting paint on the skin between them, then hang the skin back in the beaker and set the paint bar down.
context: Optical tactile fingertips for robot hands such as the open-source TacTip track white markers on the tips of pins inside a cast rubber skin; paint on the skin between the pins gives false markers. The maker's step: "Insert your thumb in the skin and press on the white paint. Make sure all the pin tips are painted white." On cast skins this is done "(painstakingly)" by hand. O*NET 17-2199.08 Robotics Engineers, core task: "Build, configure, or test robots or robotic applications."
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left); heights above the table. Skin: a cast TacTip skin (Open TacTip, Smooth-On VytaFlex 60, Shore 60A), 40 mm dome with a 25 mm skirt and a 1 mm wall, 532 pins (drawn 1.0 mm across and 2.0 mm long, estimates; tips on a 44 mm sphere in 15 rings out to 87 degrees from the apex; the cast layout is not published), turned inside out so the pins face outward, on a printed PLA painting former (fixture/painting_former.scad: 38 mm dome and body, 24 mm shank, 80 x 4 mm flange, 20 mm square handle 40 mm long; 40 g with the skin, an estimate). The former hangs by its flange on the rim of an empty Corning Pyrex 1000-250 beaker (250 mL low-form, 70 across, 95 tall; 110 g, an estimate) standing at x 235, y +195, the handle's flats turned 55 degrees; the dome's centre is 64 above the table, clear of the glass. Paint bar: clear cast acrylic square bar, 38.1 x 38.1, 152.4 long (263 g), ends faced flat, lying on the table along y, centre x 300, y -85; its +y end carries a fresh film of Humbrol Enamel No. 22 White Gloss in a 32 mm circle (about 0.15 mm, an estimate), the outer 3 mm wiped clean. Lot B is the mirror image: beaker and former at y -195 (flats at -55 degrees), bar centre at y +85 with its painted end toward -y. Nothing else is on the table. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Read from the overhead and wrist videos (frame by frame) and, after the trial, macro photos of the dome (apex and six sides), the finger pads, the beaker and the table, with a 10x loupe; the setter maps the unpainted skin's pins ring by ring before the trial. Score 0 for the whole trial if, at any moment: paint gets on the skin between the pins, the skirt or the former (a white mark 0.5 mm or more across; simulation: a press over 19 N, the dome sliding over 2 mm (while touching it with 0.1 N or more) or turning over 15 degrees in all on the wet paint within one contact, a press centred over 92 degrees from the apex, or the skirt or former within 0.5 mm of the wet circle); a gripper touches the wet paint; after the first paint, a painted pin tip touches the table, the beaker or a gripper; or the beaker tips over 30 degrees. Otherwise count white tips (half the end face or more; simulation: a tip within sqrt(F/8.3) + 0.15 mm of the face inside the 32 mm wet circle during a press of F >= 0.3 N). Every score also needs, at the end: the former hanging by its flange on the rim (upright within 8 degrees, flange within 2 mm of the rim, axis within 15 mm of the beaker's, no pin on the glass), the beaker upright within 5 degrees, its base on the table, moved 15 mm or less, the bar resting on the table with its wet circle 1 mm or more clear, both hands 30 mm or more from the former, beaker and bar, all still 1 s. 1.0: all 532 white. 0.75: 479 to 531. 0.5: 266 to 478. 0.25: 133 to 265. 0 otherwise. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged.
run_limit: 4,000 steps (200 s at 20 Hz) per trial; two trials (lots A and B)
reset_notes: 1. Wipe the bar's end with Humbrol Enamel Thinners (ventilated area), stir the paint 1 minute, brush about 0.3 mL onto the end with a 6 mm flat brush to an even film, wipe the outer 3 mm so the wet circle is 32 mm across, check 100 to 200 micrometres with a wet-film comb; start within 2 minutes. 2. Fit a fresh unpainted skin on the former, inside out, and photograph it for the pin map (one skin per trial). 3. Hang the former by its flange on the beaker's rim, flats at 55 degrees (lot B: -55), the beaker at x 235, y +195 (lot B: y -195). 4. Lay the bar with its centre at x 300, y -85, painted end toward +y (lot B: y +85, toward -y). 5. Cover the arms' finger pads with fresh nitrile finger cots. Consumed: the paint film and one skin.
fidelity: True size: 40 mm VytaFlex 60 dome, 532 pins (layout and 1 x 2 mm pins estimated), Pyrex 1000-250 beaker, 38.1 x 152.4 mm acrylic bar. The skin is rigid; its pin tips form a hemisphere collider. Paint is a declared rule: F N paints tips within sqrt(F/8.3) + 0.15 mm of the wet face (about 15 degrees of dome at 3 N; a thumb flattens a wider patch); over 19 N folds the pins; 2 mm of slide or 15 degrees of twist smears. The 0.3 mL film is not used up. A printed former replaces the thumb.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of lots A and B, 0 in each; both ran to the 4,000-step limit without refusing and painted no pin); demo: 1.0 in each of lots A and B (all 532 pins painted, no rule broken, former hung, bar set down, released and still; about 3,620 steps)
